description.value: This study investigated frontal and limbic function and connectivity during emotion down-regulation in euthymic subjects with bipolar I disorder and healthy control subjects.

Between-group results show areas of significantly increased activation in healthy control vs. euthymic subjects with bipolar I disorder during emotion down-regulation (“Decrease Negative” vs. “Observe Negative” contrast).

value: Between-group analysis revealed significantly greater activation in control compared to bipolar disorder subjects in the frontal lobe, including bilateral vlPFC, insula, bilateral MFG, bilateral cingulate and pre-SMA; other regions of greater activation in control subjects included the right IPL, bilateral MTG, bilateral lingual gyri, bilateral caudate and right thalamus. There were no areas of significantly greater activation in bipolar versus control subjects.

Between-group PPI results show significantly greater negative functional connectivity between the left amygdala and left vlPFC in healthy control vs. euthymic subjects with bipolar I disorder during emotion down-regulation (“Decrease Negative” vs. “Observe Negative”) contrast.

value: Between-group analyses using the left amygdala as a seed region revealed significantly greater negative functional connectivity in control subjects than in bipolar disorder subjects in the left vlPFC, left occipital gyrus and right posterior cingulate. The bipolar disorder greater-than-control comparison showed no significantly greater negative connectivity between the left amygdala and any regions.
